subject: Clarifying non-adaptive DPA language & subprocessor export lanes
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara@lumencare.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: DPA - non-adaptive clause + subprocessor export lanes

Karthik —

Thanks for sending the DPA draft. A couple of items our legal/procurement team flagged that we need to resolve before we can move to contracting:

1) No-adaptive / no-training language: your current clause says "Redwood will not use Customer Data to improve models unless explicit opt-in is provided." We need the contract to reflect an operational guarantee (non-adaptive) and an audit path — e.g., a statement of which subprocessors/processes will never persist training artifacts and an acceptance of an independent attestation cadence.

2) Subprocessor export lanes: Lumencare requires that any data leaving the EU/US (where applicable) be routed only through approved export lanes (SFTP onshore, regional KMS, or direct VPC-only processing). We want an explicit mapping for the subprocessors you list in Appendix B to the export lanes so we can validate residency and export controls.

3) Prompt/response ownership: we need a short confirmatory sentence that Lumencare retains ownership of prompts and outputs and that Redwood will not assert derivative IP beyond running inference to serve responses back to Lumencare.

We can do a one-hour call with procurement + legal if that helps. I attached our redlines. Can you propose either contract language or operational artifacts (attestation certificate / subprocessor mapping) we can review?

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Patel
Head of Legal Operations
Lumencare

Attachment: lumencare-dpa-redlines.pdf (annotation summary)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA - non-adaptive clause + subprocessor export lanes

Sara —

Appreciate the detailed redlines. Quick answers and an ask for follow-up: 

1) No-adaptive / no-training guarantee: we can commit to a "non-adaptive processing" operational guarantee for Lumencare's production tenant (we will not use Customer Data to improve general models or persistent model weights). Operationally, this maps to: ephemeral KV caching only, no training dataset persistence, and production tenant isolation.

2) Attestation cadence: we can provide quarterly attestation scoped to the on-premises/hosted controls listed in the DPA (SOC2 + an additional no-training attestation). Kimberly — can you confirm standard attestation template and expected evidence (audit log snippets / no-train toggle config exports)?

3) Subprocessor export lanes: we maintain a subprocessor inventory and can produce a mapping to export lanes (SFTP onshore, onshore KMS, VPC-only) per subprocessor. David — can you prepare a one-page mapping and the short explanation of how we enforce export lanes (routing policy + fallback).

4) Prompt/response ownership: Redwood can include the sentence Lumencare requested: "Customer retains ownership of prompts and outputs; Redwood does not acquire derivative IP rights to Customer-provided prompts or generated outputs beyond delivering inference services." Legal: we prefer the wording "does not assert derivative IP rights." Let me know if that is acceptable to Lumencare legal.

We can also do a 30–45 minute sync to walk through the mapping and attestation samples. Proposed times: Tue 9/1 10:00–10:45 PT or Wed 9/2 8:30–9:15 PT.

-Karthik
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Policy
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the redlines and the call offer. Short operational reply in case it helps the packet you present to procurement: 

1) Enforcement: We use tenant-scoped routing tags at the API gateway and an enforcement layer in the runtime that guarantees data tagged as Lumencare-production is only processed on pinned pools or VPC networks. For non-VPC customers we use an onshore SFTP export lane for archival exports and an onshore KMS for any keying material related to Lumencare.

2) Export lane mapping (high level):
- Subprocessor: Storage-Connector Inc. -> Region: US -> Export lane: SFTP_onshore
- Subprocessor: MetricsPipeline Ltd. -> Region: EU -> Export lane: VPC_only
- Subprocessor: LoggingCorp -> Region: US -> Export lane: KMS_onshore

3) No-train verification: We will provide an attestation package quarterly showing (a) no-persistent-training flag set for your tenant, (b) sampled audit logs showing no write operations to training stores, and (c) a signed statement from our infra team about KV cache transience policies. We will redact internal IP but include sufficient identifiers for procurement to validate controls.

If the mapping above works, Karthik — can you include the proposed contract sentence for prompt/response ownership and a clause referencing the attestation cadence? Sara — if you prefer, we can join the Tue 10:00 PT slot for a 30-minute walk-through; Kimberly can share the attestation template live.
